/--
Prove that $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ has no proper subgroups of finite index.
-/
theorem eq_top_of_finiteIndex (H : AddSubgroup (ℚ ⧸ (Int.castAddHom ℚ).range)) (h_fin : H.FiniteIndex) :
    H = ⊤ := by
  rw [eq_top_iff]
  intro x _
  set n := H.index with hn_def
  have hn : n ≠ 0 := h_fin.finiteIndex
  -- Step 1: n • z ∈ H for every z
  have key : ∀ z : ℚ ⧸ (Int.castAddHom ℚ).range, n • z ∈ H := by
    intro z
    exact H.nsmul_index_mem z
  -- Step 2: ℚ/ℤ is divisible, so there exists y with n • y = x
  induction x using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on with
  | H q =>
    set y : ℚ ⧸ (Int.castAddHom ℚ).range :=
      QuotientAddGroup.mk ((q : ℚ) / (n : ℚ)) with hy_def
    have hny : n • y = QuotientAddGroup.mk q := by
      simp only [hy_def]
      rw [← QuotientAddGroup.mk_nsmul]
      congr 1
      field_simp
    have hmem : QuotientAddGroup.mk q ∈ H := by
      rw [← hny]
      exact key y
    exact hmem
